messages:
Sam (AE): Heads up — Marina's POC returned with a multi-entity billing request. They want Order Forms signed for two legal entities + a 5%/90d holdback. Also their bank wiring requires payment to a separate payor entity. Need legal + finance guidance, can we do this and how to route signatures?

Priya (Sales Ops): We rarely do per-entity OFs but we've carved this before. Sam, can you share the counterparty tax IDs and the exact holdback language?

Sam (AE): Uploaded the doc they sent: https://acme.example.com/poc/order/attachments — holdback text: `5% holdback for 90 days` and "final payment to Payor Entity B" is explicit.

Marina (Customer): Correct. POC will be billed to Entity A, compliance requires the final payment from Entity B. They want Redwood to sign corresponding OFs for each entity and accept the holdback.

Jordan (Legal): We can support dual-entity arrangements but prefer a single MSA that covers both entities instead of separate MSAs. Recommended redline to OF: add a clause clarifying Billing vs Payor entity and require evidence of intercompany agreement. For the holdback, we need release tied to acceptance criteria — otherwise cap liability.

Kenji (Finance): Wiring to a different payor is acceptable if legal docs match. We'll need W-9/W-8 per entity and the bank form with payee details. Note: a 5% holdback will defer revenue recognition; FYI tax team needs to review. 30-day net still expected unless they request change.

Sam (AE): Jordan — can you paste a short sample redline we can send to the customer? They're pushing for signatures by EOD.

Jordan (Legal): Sample OF paragraph to propose: `Where Customer is comprised of multiple legal entities, the Order Form's specified Billing Entity shall be the sole entity invoiced; Redwood will accept wiring instructions to a separate Payor entity subject to evidence of an intercompany agreement and execution of this Order Form by an authorized signatory. Any contractual holdback shall be limited to 5% and released upon written acceptance of deliverables or upon mutual written agreement. Redwood reserves the right to cap total holdback exposure to an amount not to exceed the value of the services rendered during the POC.`

Priya (Sales Ops): DocuSign flow question — they want simultaneous signing by both entities (parallel lane). We support parallel signing. Sam, do you have both signer emails so I can set up the envelope? Also I can add an internal checkbox for "holdback on OF" to route to Finance automatically.

Sam (AE): I have finance@entityb.com and legal@entitya.com. I'll add them to the envelope. Marina — can you confirm authorized signers and provide W-9/W-8?

Marina (Customer): Finance and Legal are authorized. I'll attach W9 for Entity A and W8 for Entity B to the DocuSign envelope.

LegalBot: Reference template: https://internal.redwood/legal/templates/orderform-multi-entity-redline-v2.pdf :point_right: Jordan, please confirm final redline upload when ready.

Jordan (Legal): I'll finalize the redline and upload in 30 mins. Short answer: we can proceed with parallel DocuSign, include the Billing/Payor clause and acceptance-tied holdback release. Sam — collect the entity docs and I'll add a one-paragraph redline to the OF.

Kenji (Finance): Finance provisionally approves subject to receiving W-9/W-8 and intercompany agreement. Marking transaction as "needs-docs" and flagging revenue recognition impact.

Sam (AE): Got it — will bundle docs + redline, route DocuSign with parallel lanes. ETA: EOD. :thumbsup:

Priya (Sales Ops): Marking this thread `needs-legal` and `needs-finance` in SFDC. I'll also create the internal ticket for the orderform routing.
